correctness.rationale: Cubic geometric singularity is exactly a projective common zero of the three quadratic partials by Euler identity in characteristic two. Three quadrics with empty projective zero locus form a homogeneous regular sequence, and the Hilbert series (1+t)^3 makes the degree-four Macaulay map onto; conversely surjectivity forbids a common projective zero. Hence rank 15 is a necessary and sufficient absolute geometric test. The 1023 nonzero cubics, 5544 compatible pencils, 864 unique septuple nets, zero four-generator extensions, 168 projective substitutions and seven rational point evaluations form fully explicit exhaustive finite loops. The complete standalone checker executed and asserted 864, eight orbits with sizes 168 five times and 8 three times, and five spectra. An independently coded geometric gradient check over F2,F4,F8,F16 corroborates the count of 336 individual smooth cubics but is not relied upon as a complete smoothness proof. No infinite claim rests on a finite-extension experiment.

originality.rationale: The sharp maximum projective dimension two for smooth cubic nets over F2, and existence, were already established by Asgarli--Ghioca--Reichstein; they are not claimed original. The newly assessed claim is the complete exact enumeration of 864 maximal nets, their eight PGL3(F2) orbit classes, five exact seven-member rational-point spectra and absence of rational base points. The primary papers actually inspected discuss existence, maximum dimension, individual cubics, weaker geometric irreducibility or GIT stability, none of which logically implies these exact new classification data. The residual risk is an unindexed independent enumeration, not an identified dominating result.
residual_risks: No absolute priority or nonexistence of an unindexed equivalent net census can be certified by literature/database search.
The six-file package has self-review and runnable exact code, not independent external mathematical validation.
The exact count concerns projective classes of nets; it does not classify the isomorphism types of all individual member curves.

value.rationale: The maximal smooth-cubic net dimension is already a natural, motivated published problem. Once the maximum is known, its complete extremal space and projective-moduli quotient are substantive canonical finite classification invariants: exactly 864 nets, eight orbit types, five arithmetic member spectra and rational base-point freeness. These distinguish maximal constructions beyond existence and are neither arbitrary parameter slices nor a recomputation of the known 336 individual cubic forms. No downstream theorem or publication-scale contribution is required for these exact natural moduli counts.
